title: The 2020 warm offset of Navy MetOp-A v2.0 SST that steps DOISST v2.1 comes from daytime pixel selection, not retrieval coefficients; DOISST satellite-count changes (2007-2021) do not step its mean
abstract: Question: the 7 July 2020 warm step in NOAA Daily OISST v2.1 (DOISST) starts when the Navy (NAVO) MetOp-A AVHRR L2P input changed from processing v1.0 to v2.0 (sci:sha256:9fca62cd). Which part of the new processing makes the input warmer: new retrieval coefficients or a new selection of pixels? And do other input changes step DOISST? Approach: (A) we streamed 418 NAVO MetOp-A granules with brightness temperatures (21 June-5 July and 7-21 July, 2020 and 2019 as a control), fitted a split-window retrieval to v1.0 pixels and applied it to v2.0 pixels, and used 3,232 and 2,831 match-ups with drifting and moored buoys (iQuam). (B) We found input-density events as steps in the DOISST analysis-error field (2006-2021, NOAA ERDDAP) and tested them against steps of DOISST minus ESA SST CCI. Results: against buoys the v2.0 offset is +0.080 C (95% interval 0.039 to 0.117; 2020 minus 2019): +0.154 C by day and -0.009 C at night. For the same radiances the retrieval gives only +0.016 C (-0.007 to +0.041) more; the selected pixels are +0.102 C warmer (by day +0.179 C, at night +0.001 C). By day all percentiles move up (median +0.17 C); at night v2.0 keeps more cold outliers. At 22 error events the DOISST minus CCI step has a mean percentile of 49 (null 50, p = 0.56); the 2007 Pathfinder-to-Navy change (error z = -7.7) gives -0.005 C, and the 2020 step does not show in the error field. A 3-week episode in November 2013 is real (DOISST minus drifters +0.056 C), with no matching NAVO stream change. Conclusion: the 2020 step comes from daytime pixel screening in NAVO v2.0; gains or losses of satellites do not step the DOISST mean, but bias changes do, and data-count diagnostics cannot find them. Limitations: the retrieval emulator reproduces v1.0 only to 0.21-0.34 C per pixel; we cannot tell diurnal warm layers from contamination; DOISST input files are not public; the 2013 input is unidentified.

citations.reason: Identified the NAVO v1.0-to-v2.0 change as the cause of the 2020 step; we use its windows and stream dates, confirm the offset against buoys and find its mechanism (daytime selection). At buoy match-ups we find no night offset, unlike its +0.08 C night offset against CCI bins.
We use its daily DOISST minus ESA CCI regional series 1982-2024 for the input-event audit.
